title: Shared responsibility: AWS or Cairnway?
description: Sort each security job for Cairnway's Bedrock chatbot: does AWS handle it, or does Cairnway?

items.text: Physical security of the data centres that run Amazon Bedrock.
items.why: AWS protects the infrastructure that runs all of its services, including the buildings.

items.text: Deciding which IAM roles may call the Bedrock model.
items.why: Access to your account's resources is your configuration. Least privilege is your job.

items.text: Running and patching the servers behind the Bedrock service itself.
items.why: Bedrock is a managed service, so AWS runs and maintains the servers that host it.

items.text: Choosing to encrypt the knowledge-base data with a KMS key Cairnway manages.
items.why: Encryption choices for your data and resources are part of the security configuration you control.

items.text: Configuring guardrails so the chatbot refuses off-topic or harmful requests.
items.why: Guardrails are a tool AWS provides, but setting them up for your application is your responsibility.

items.text: Checking the documents fed to the chatbot for customers' personal data.
items.why: You control your content: what data goes in and whether it is sensitive.

items.text: Turning on model invocation logging to keep prompts and responses.
items.why: Invocation logging is off by default; enabling it is your choice and configuration.

items.text: Maintaining the global network that connects AWS Regions and data centres.
items.why: The network infrastructure of the AWS Cloud is part of the security of the cloud, which AWS owns.

items.text: Patching the operating system of EC2 instances where Cairnway hosts its own open-source model.
items.why: On EC2 you manage the guest operating system, so its patches are yours. Compare this with Bedrock, where AWS runs the servers.

items.text: Securing the hardware and virtualization layer under every EC2 instance.
items.why: AWS protects the hardware and the software that runs the cloud, whatever you run on top.

items.text: Reviewing whether the chatbot's answers are accurate and fair before launch.
items.why: How you use a model and whether its output fits your purpose are your responsibility.

items.text: Deciding who in the company may read the chatbot's conversation logs.
items.why: Access to your own data, logs included, is controlled by your IAM and bucket policies.
